test_title: PYST 38: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which property is shown by ethanol?

options.text: It has a sweet smell and is volatile
It forms scum with hard water
It is solid at room temperature

solution:
The correct answer is __**It has a sweet smell and is volatile**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethanol**, also known as **ethyl alcohol**, is a colorless liquid that possesses a distinct, **pleasant sweet smell** and a characteristic burning taste.
 
• It is a highly **volatile** substance, which means it evaporates rapidly at **standard temperature and pressure** due to its relatively low **boiling point** of **78.37°C** (**351.5 K**). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The formation of **scum** (insoluble precipitates) is a property of **soap** reacting with **calcium** and **magnesium ions** in **hard water**. **Ethanol** is a covalent organic compound and does not react with these ions to form scum. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Ethanol** has a very low **melting point** of **-114.1°C** (**159 K**). Consequently, it exists in a **liquid state** at **room temperature** (approx **25°C**) and does not solidify under normal environmental conditions. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Chemically, **ethanol** is **neutral** in nature. Although its formula **C2H5OH** contains a **hydroxyl group**, it does not ionize in water to release **hydroxide ions** (OH-), nor does it change the color of **litmus paper**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is It has a sweet smell and is volatile.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Nature and Formula**: **Ethanol** is a **primary alcohol** with the chemical formula **C2H5OH**. It is the second member of the **homologous series** of alcohols.
 
• **Solubility**: It is **highly soluble** in **water** in all proportions. This solubility is due to the ability of the **hydroxyl group** in ethanol to form **hydrogen bonds** with **water molecules**.
 
• **Combustion**: It is a **flammable** liquid that burns with a clean **blue flame**. The reaction produces **carbon dioxide** and **water vapor**, releasing a significant amount of **energy**.
 
• **Applications as Fuel**: Because it is a **renewable** source of energy (often produced from **biomass**), it is used as an **additive in petrol**. In **India**, the **Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme** aims to increase the blend percentage to **20%** (**E20**) by the **year 2025**.
 
• **Industrial Uses**: It serves as a versatile **solvent** in the manufacture of **paints**, **varnishes**, **perfumes**, and **medicines** like **tincture of iodine** and **cough syrups**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reaction with Sodium**: When **ethanol** reacts with **sodium metal**, it evolves **hydrogen gas** and forms **sodium ethoxide**. This reaction is often used as a **chemical test** for the presence of the **alcoholic group**.
 
• **Oxidation**: Upon heating with **alkaline potassium permanganate** or **acidified potassium dichromate**, ethanol undergoes **oxidation** to form **ethanoic acid** (**acetic acid**).
 
• **Denatured Alcohol**: To prevent the **illegal consumption** of industrial-grade ethanol, it is made unfit for drinking by adding poisonous substances like **methanol** or **pyridine** and dyes like **copper sulphate** to give it a blue color. This is known as **denaturation**.
 
• **Medical Use**: In a concentration of **70%**, it is an effective **antiseptic** used in **hand sanitizers** to kill **microorganisms** by denaturing their **proteins** and dissolving their **lipid membranes**.
